label: early copy phase (recall 0-3), weak preference for input h/i
explanation: Almost never fires in the original phase (4 of 12.8k dev activations). Activity sits in the delimiter step and the first few copy steps: recall_idx 0-3 holds about 94% of activation mass, peaking at recall_idx 1-2 (t=9-11), and it is more frequent in longer sequences (L=9 holds 39% of mass). Inside that window it fires on only ~3% of steps, so position alone is a base-rate description (F1 0.06). Token preferences are spread out: input h (6.8x lift) and i (4.4x), next output i/l/h/x/d/o/m (4-6x). Adding h/i input and L>=6 gives the best dev F1 (0.24, precision 0.30, recall 0.21). Larger activations go with input h/i early in the copy phase (top examples: copying h or i at recall 1-2), but most activations are small and spread across many tokens. No single coherent predicate covers it.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=11: h, i, v, k; t=13: h, i, p, k; t=5: i, h, d, v) and the next token to output (most: i, l, h, x, o, m; least: -, t, y, j); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=2, recall_idx=1, L=9 & t=12.
